turnPlan.question: Explain Le Chatelier's principle using the Haber process when pressure increases.

qualitativeClaims.claim: Le Chatelier's principle: when a constraint (change of pressure, temperature or concentration) is imposed on a system at equilibrium, the system adjusts to oppose that change and restore equilibrium.
Haber process equilibrium: N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g); 4 moles of gas on the left, 2 moles of gas on the right.
qualitativeClaims.expected: 4 mol gas reactants vs 2 mol gas product

qualitativeClaims.claim: When pressure is increased, the equilibrium shifts to the side with fewer moles of gas to reduce the pressure.
For the Haber process, increased pressure shifts equilibrium to the right (forward direction), producing more NH3.
qualitativeClaims.expected: Forward shift, yield of NH3 increases

qualitativeClaims.claim: The position of equilibrium moves right but the equilibrium constant K is unchanged because temperature is unchanged.
Industrially this is why the Haber process uses high pressure (about 200 atm), favouring ammonia yield.

assumptions: Gases behave ideally so mole ratio determines pressure response
Temperature held constant when pressure is changed
